pages.quiz:
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

9. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

3. C — 100 °C

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

5. C — Ice melting to water

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

8. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

9. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

11. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

12. A — Glucose and oxygen

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Slopes as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Invertebrates; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
